title: Nothing technically stops a direct hand-edit of .quest/*.json, bypassing CLI validation
description:
CLAUDE.md instructs every session not to edit .quest/ task, draft, document, decision or milestone JSON files directly, and to use the quest CLI instead -- but this is convention only. Verified by reading the code: LocalTaskRepository writes plain files via node fs writeFile with no filesystem permission restriction, no pre-commit hook, and no git-level enforcement anywhere in this repository blocking a text editor from touching .quest/tasks/*.json directly.

The only existing backstop is the Tracker integrity CI check (.github/workflows/tracker-integrity.yml), whose first real assertion is that `quest task list --json` succeeds. That catches a hand-edit that breaks JSON parsing, produces a duplicate id, or otherwise fails taskState/validate -- but only at PR/push time, not locally, and only for defects an automated check can see. It cannot catch a syntactically valid hand-edit that lies about something no automated check can verify -- for example, flipping an acceptance-criterion checked flag to true with no real evidence behind it, which is exactly the kind of write the quest CLI does not prevent either, but at least routes through one code path where the intent (task-finalization guidance: a criterion checked on faith is worse than one left open) is documented and can be taught to, reviewed, or audited by actor id.

This is a real, not hypothetical, gap: this same session separately had to correct a shell-quoting mistake (unescaped backticks in a double-quoted --description argument triggering bash command substitution) that could have caused unintended tracker state, caught only by reading the created record back. A more disciplined write path -- CLI-only, or at least CLI-preferred with a cheap local guard -- would narrow that whole class of accident, not just this one instance of it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A decision is made and recorded on the enforcement mechanism (a local pre-commit hook rejecting a staged .quest/*.json change not produced by the quest CLI; a repo-level technical restriction; or an explicit reason the current CI-only, convention-backed approach is accepted as sufficient)
If a mechanism is implemented, it is demonstrated: a direct hand-edit of a .quest/*.json file is rejected (locally, pre-commit) or flagged, distinct from a quest-CLI-produced change to the same file

The decision accounts for legitimate non-CLI touches to .quest/ that already exist in this repository (for example the documented sanctioned exception for removing a genuine duplicate-id record by hand, per src/cli/main.ts near line 3044) so a new gate does not block a case CLAUDE.md already permits
